blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz narrates that a man from the Muraad tribe once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA) when he was busy performing salaah in the Masjid. (After Hadhrat Ali (RA) completed the salaah) The man said to him, "Appoint some guards because the people of the Muraad tribe are planning to assassinate you." However, he said to them, "Two angels are assigned to each and every person to protect him from that which is not destined for him. However, when something predestined comes his way, the two angels leave him to it. One's appointed term is a fortified shield (because nothing can violate it)."[^1]
Hadhrat Yahya bin Katheer and others report that when people offered to guard Hadhrat Ali (RA), he said, "A person's appointed term guards him."[^2]

Hadhrat Muhammad Baaqir reports that two men presented their dispute to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for judgement. When he sat at the base of a wall, one of the men cautioned, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! That wall is going to fall." Hadhrat Ali (RA) reassured him saying, "Continue. Allaah suffices as a protector." When Hadhrat Ali (RA) had passed judgment and stood up, the wall fell down.[^3]
The Tawakkul of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Dhabiyya reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was on his deathbed, Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) visited him. "What is the problem?" Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) asked. "My problem is my sins," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) asked further, "What do you wish for?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "For the mercy of my Rabb." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then asked, "Should I not have a physician see you?" (Referring to the fact that Allaah is the greatest of curers,) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "It was the physician (Allaah) Who gave me the illness."
Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) further asked, "Should I then not have an allowance fixed." "I have no need for an allowance," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) assured him. "But it would belong to your daughters after your demise," Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) explained. "Do you fear that my daughters would suffer poverty after my death?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) asked in surprise. He then continued, "I have instructed my daughters to recite Surah Waaqi'ah every night because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that poverty shall never ever afflict the person who recites Surah Waaqi'ah every night."[^4]
Incidents similar to this concerning Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) have passed in the chapter concerning exercising patience during illness.
Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.88).
